title: How Much Does It Cost to Carpet Stairs in Seattle?
meta: Carpet on stairs costs $30 per step in labor at Wills Flooring, so a 13-step Seattle staircase is $390 plus carpet and pad. See what else moves the quote.
keywords: cost to carpet stairs Seattle, carpet stairs price per step, how much to carpet a staircase, stair carpet installation Seattle WA, waterfall vs Hollywood stair carpet cost

blocks.lead: Carpeting stairs in Seattle costs $30 per step in labor at Wills Flooring, so a straight 13-step staircase is 13 x $30 = $390, plus the carpet and pad.
blocks.detail: Landings and pie-shaped winders each count as a step. Pulling the old carpet, pad and staples out adds $0.45 per sq ft, about $27 on a 13-step flight. The carpet and pad themselves are quoted at the free in-home estimate, because material is what really moves the number.

blocks.html: Seattle is a staircase city. Wallingford and Ballard split-levels have a short run up and a short run down, Queen Anne and Capitol Hill houses have steep, narrow flights with a turn, and every townhome from Beacon Hill to Magnolia has three floors of stairs. Stairs are quoted differently from rooms, so here is what goes into the number and how to count your own steps.

blocks.text: Why stairs are priced per step instead of per square foot

items.title: Every step is cut and fitted by hand
items.text: A bedroom is one big piece stretched to the walls. A staircase is thirteen or more small pieces, each cut, padded, stapled at the crotch of the riser and trimmed to the stringer. Labor per square foot is several times a flat room, which is why stairs are counted by the step.

items.title: Waste is high
items.text: Carpet comes 12 ft wide. A 3 ft stair uses strips cut from that roll, and patterns have to be matched on every step. A staircase eats a surprising amount of carpet for its footprint, and that waste shows up on the material line.

items.title: Shape changes everything
items.text: A pie-shaped winder takes twice as long as a straight tread, and an open-sided stair means wrapping the nosing around the end of each tread. The rate stays $30, but the day gets longer, so tell us the shape when you call.

items.title: Old Seattle stairs are rarely square
items.text: Craftsman and Tudor staircases have settled for a century. Treads are out of level, risers vary in height and nosings are worn round. Good installers pad and stretch to hide it. Fast installers leave puckers you see every time you climb.

rows: Every step is a unit of labor, and a landing counts as one. Sixteen steps plus a landing is 17 x $30 = $510.
A pie step is patterned, cut and matched individually, so it takes longer, but we still bill it at $30. The time shows up in the schedule, not the price.
The carpet wraps under the nosing and the edge is finished by hand. It is slower work at the same per-step price.
Hollywood tucks the carpet tight under each nosing for a tailored look and takes longer than a waterfall drape. Both are $30 per step.
Material is the biggest variable in any carpet quote. Patterns need matching on every step, and a staircase wastes more carpet than its footprint suggests.
Old carpet, tack strip and hundreds of staples. A 13-step flight measures about 60 sq ft, so roughly $27 to strip and haul away.

blocks.text: Waterfall vs Hollywood: the look and the labor

a.title: Choose waterfall when
items: You want the lower labor cost and a softer, more casual look
The carpet is a Berber or loop that does not bend crisply
Nosings are worn round on an older Seattle staircase
The stairs are enclosed on both sides

b.title: Choose Hollywood when
items: You want the tailored, upholstered look buyers expect in Queen Anne or Magnolia
The carpet is a cut pile or a pattern that shows the nosing line
One or both sides are open with a banister
You are pairing carpet stairs with hardwood floors above and below

blocks.text: How stair carpet compares to hardwood or vinyl plank on stairs

blocks.html: Stairs are the one place where the three floors we install are easy to compare, because all three are billed per step. Wills Flooring installs hardwood on stairs at $125 per stair, vinyl plank or laminate at $100 per stair and carpet at $30 per step, labor only. On a 13-step Seattle staircase that is $1,625, $1,300 or $390. Material narrows the gap, since hardwood treads cost more than a strip of carpet, but carpet stays the cheapest way to cover a flight.

blocks.title: Seattle condo and townhome note:
blocks.text: Many Capitol Hill and Belltown buildings require carpet on stairs and upper floors for sound. If your HOA has an acoustic rule, ask for the required pad rating before you shop. We bring the spec sheet for the building manager and handle the elevator reservation on install day.
What a Seattle stair install day looks like

items.text: Old carpet, pad, tack strip and staples come out. On 1920s to 1950s houses we check whether the treads are fir or oak you might want refinished instead.

items.d: Pad and tack strip, about 1 hour
items.text: New pad is cut and stapled per tread with a gap at the nosing. Tack strip goes at the crotch of each riser for a stretch-in stair.
Each step is stretched with a knee kicker, stapled, and trimmed. Hollywood wraps add time. Pie treads and open sides add more.
Landings are seamed last so the pattern runs true. You can walk on the stairs immediately.
items.note: A straight run is done by early afternoon; a turned, open staircase is a full day.

blocks.text: How to get an honest stair carpet quote in Seattle

items.html: Count your treads before anyone visits. Include landings and note which steps are pie-shaped or open on a side. At $30 a step, that count is most of your labor number.
Ask for the wrap method on the quote. Waterfall and Hollywood should be named, because they are different amounts of work and look different.
Pick a stair-rated carpet. Dense low pile, nylon or triexta, holds up to the concentrated wear on stair nosings far better than a soft plush. Our best carpet for stairs post explains why.
Ask what is under the old carpet. Many Ballard and Wallingford stairs hide finished fir treads. Refinishing them at $55 to $75 per tread is sometimes the better call than new carpet.
Insist on a firm written number. We measure every step, bring the samples and write the price on the spot, backed by a 1-year workmanship warranty. See what the carpet installation visit includes.

faq.q: How is carpet for stairs priced?
faq.a: By the step. Wills Flooring charges $30 per step in labor, counting landings and pie-shaped winders as steps, plus $0.45 per sq ft to tear out the old carpet and pad. The carpet and pad go on a separate line, quoted at the free estimate once you have picked a style off the samples.

faq.q: How much carpet do I need for 13 stairs?
faq.a: A typical closed stair with 3 ft treads uses roughly 18 to 20 inches of carpet per step, so 13 steps need about 20 to 22 linear feet cut from a 12 ft roll. Pie treads, open sides and pattern matching add to that. Labor is a flat 13 x $30 = $390 either way.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to carpet stairs or install hardwood on them?
faq.a: In labor, carpet is far cheaper. We install carpet on stairs at $30 per step, vinyl plank at $100 and hardwood at $125, so a 13-step flight is $390, $1,300 or $1,625 in labor. Material closes some of that gap, but carpet stays the least expensive way to finish a staircase.

faq.q: What is the difference between waterfall and Hollywood stair carpet?
faq.a: Waterfall drapes the carpet over each nosing and straight down the riser in one flow, which is faster and suits loops and Berbers. Hollywood, also called cap and band, wraps the carpet tightly under the nosing for a tailored, upholstered edge. Hollywood takes longer and costs more in labor.

faq.q: How long does it take to carpet a staircase?
faq.a: A straight 13-step staircase takes about half a day including tear-out. A staircase with a turn, pie-shaped treads, open sides or a landing can take a full day. You can use the stairs as soon as the installer finishes; there is no cure time with stretch-in carpet.

faq.q: Do Seattle condos require carpet on stairs?
faq.a: Many do. Multi-level condos and townhomes in Capitol Hill, Belltown and Queen Anne often have HOA acoustic rules requiring carpet and a rated pad on stairs and upper floors. Ask for the required pad rating before choosing, and we will bring the specification sheet for the building to approve.
